summary: @wololasod/tiny-id fetches and executes remote scripts from attacker-controlled hosts on require
details: On require of the package's main entry, the module re-spawns itself detached with an environment variable that gates a payload branch, then downloads a platform-specific script from attacker-controlled hosts — https://peppy-cranachan-2c35bd.netlify.app/ontwimbiti.ps1 on Windows and https://kraken-fun.netlify.app/linuxyesus.py on Linux — writes it to a temp path under a cover filename (nupkg_system.diagnostics.performancecounter.8.0.0.ps1/.py) intended to look like a NuGet/.NET artifact, executes it, and deletes the file. The Windows branch invokes PowerShell with -WindowStyle Hidden -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -NoProfile and spawns detached with stdio ignored to suppress output and bypass policy. The fetch-and-execute behavior is unrelated to the advertised ID-generation purpose and fires at module load time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
